messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated SRV lookup error rate from service-discovery (CoreDNS) in us-east2 region. Affected zone: us-east2b. https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/9876

sre-bot: Prometheus alert firing: srv_lookup_fail_rate > 5% for 3min. Error patterns show SERVFAIL and timeout for SRV queries to consul backend from model-serving fleet (us-east2b).

kai: oncall here. seeing spike in 5xx from model-ingress in us-east2b, correlates with service discovery errors. paging net-oncall and infra.

maria: flagged support cases from 2 enterprise customers with increased inference latency and connection retries, looks like client side falling back then hitting capacity elsewhere. estimated impact: ~4-7% requests failing for us-east2b.

net-oncall: pinged. seeing intermittent GRE tunnel flaps between us-east2b <-> us-east2a on our overlay. BGP session is up but we have packet loss on specific paths for UDP (DNS).

emma: can we verify CoreDNS pod logs? might be upstream forwarders dropping EDNS0 or large response UDP fragments.

raj: grabbing logs. relevant lines: 
```
2026-03-15T07:20:03Z coredns[0]: lookup _redwood._tcp.svc.cluster.local. IN SRV: error SERVFAIL from 10.100.2.3
2026-03-15T07:20:05Z coredns[1]: upstream timeout to 10.200.1.5:53
```
looks like coredns is forwarding to consul resolvers which are getting UDP packet loss.

kai: quick mitigation options: 1) restart coredns pods (force new connections to healthy forwarders) 2) increase coredns replicas + enable tcp fallback 3) steer service traffic away from us-east2b at L4 load-balancer for a short window. preference: steer traffic while we stabilize.

emma: agree. start with steering critical model-serving routes to us-east2a and scale coredns to 3 replicas in us-east2b, then restart coredns one-by-one. I'll take the L4 change.

emma: taking action: edited internal-nyx-lb weights to prefer us-east2a (10%->80% weight) for model-serving routes. command: `infractl lb update --service model-ingress --region us-east2 --weights a=80,b=20`

maria: posting customer update: "We're investigating increased inference errors in us-east2b, traffic is being routed to alternate zone while we mitigate. No data exposure. Will post follow-up in 30m." :spiral_note_pad:

raj: scaling coredns in kube: `kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy coredns --replicas=3 --context=us-east2b`

kai: rolling restart coredns pods one at a time: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deploy/coredns` (doing now).

sre-bot: Deploy bot: rollout of coredns started (deploy/coredns) — pods restarting across nodes.

net-oncall: still seeing packet drops on UDP path, but less frequent after diverting L4 traffic. GRE tunnel shows interface flaps at 07:22:11 UTC, suspected MTU mismatch + fragmentation of DNS responses (EDNS0).

raj: quick config tweak: enable `proxy` plugin tcp fallback in coredns configmap and set `max_concurrent 1000` for forwarding. applying now. snippet:
```
forward . 10.200.1.5 10.200.1.6 {
  policy sequential
  max_concurrent 1000
}
transport tcp
```

emma: applied tcp fallback and updated configmap, restarting coredns to pick up.

maria: monitoring customer error graphs — backend errors dropping from ~6% -> ~1.2% over last 6 minutes. posting interim update to cases.

kai: good. next step: network to remediate GRE tunnel. net-oncall, can you patch MTU and rekey the tunnel?

net-oncall: scheduling tunnel maintenance, will bump MTU and switch to TCP encapsulation for control plane for 15min. doing rekey at 07:30 UTC. Expect brief packet loss during rekey.

raj: observing CoreDNS logs now show fewer upstream timeouts. also seeing consul DNS responses arrive over TCP fallback.

sre-bot: Incident timeline note: diversion at 07:21 UTC, scale + tcp-fallback at 07:24 UTC, tunnel rekey planned 07:30 UTC.

maria: customer update posted: "Routing adjusted and mitigation in progress. Some customers saw degraded latency while traffic shifted; errors are decreasing. We're keeping the incident open and will follow up with root cause once network fix completes." :thumbsup:

emma: handoff note: I need to transfer on-call to Kai at 08:00 UTC. Kai, you'll take lead for the postmortem and final closure.

kai: taking handoff. will coordinate postmortem, collect packet captures, GRE tunnel history, CoreDNS forwarder metrics, and consul logs. assign to incident owner tag: #INC-2026-332.

net-oncall: tunnel MTU patched and rekeyed at 07:33 UTC. observed no further flaps. UDP path stable.

raj: final check: service discovery error rate back to baseline ~0.3%. model-serving 5xx back to normal.

maria: closing customer-facing note: "Issue mitigated; further engineering follow-up scheduled. We'll share RCA and timeline within 48 hours." 

kai: moving to post-incident phase. created task list: packet captures + MTU diff, CoreDNS config diff, consul backend health checks, and test plan to validate EDNS0 fragmentation. will schedule follow-up on-call review. :spiral_calendar_pad:

sre-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident owner: kai.

emma: thanks everyone. great quick coordination. :heart:
